counters.name: guardrails-posttooluse-run-guards-spawns
counters.command:
bash scripts/hook-census.sh guardrails PostToolUse cli-flag-verify.sh '{"session_id":"census","hook_event_name":"PostToolUse","cwd":"@DIR@","tool_name":"Edit","tool_input":{"file_path":"@DIR@/README.md","old_string":"Census","new_string":"See `docs/old.md`."},"tool_response":{"filePath":"@DIR@/README.md","success":true}}' --setup 'g() { git -c user.name=census -c user.email=census@example.invalid "$@"; }; mkdir docs && echo x >docs/old.md && g add docs/old.md && g commit -qm add && g rm -q docs/old.md && g commit -qm rm && printf "# Title

See \140docs/old.md\140.
" >README.md' --check 'grep -qF "STALE_PATH: docs/old.md" "$HOOK_STDOUT"'
counters.goal: The PostToolUse Edit(*.md) verify bundle (cli-flag-verify, skill-reference-verify, stale-path-verify through run-guards.sh) spends at most this many process creations and execs on an Edit whose new text cites a path the repository deleted. #4390 measured 87 processes per PostToolUse:Edit fire on Windows. The count includes every process git starts itself, so a runner image that changes git can move it. Parsing the payload once brought a Linux census to 38. Reusing the deleted-path set brought the cold finding fire to 25. Counting a non-word anchor in-process and reading the skip-worktree tag without tr or cut brought it to 19: the shell, the dispatcher, and five git processes. Exec form launches that row through node, which adds one process (#3686). The 2026-09-28 Linux census measured 20. The ratchet step prints the current versions. Correlation: unproven: CPU dominates on Linux CI (plugins/guardrails/reference/edit-write-guards/PLAN.md)
